_meta.description: Impact-to-priority rubric (#2992). Read by /bug to derive a filing priority, by the severity-proportionate review criterion to judge one, and by /resolve-review to propose a correction. Replaces /bug's fixed --priority p1 (#1520), whose 'bugs are more urgent than enhancements' still holds for broken behavior on a supported path — kept here as p1/p0 — but overstated urgency for the advisory and dev-only bugs that dominated the 2026-09-22 criteria audit.

precedence: Evaluate every class against the bug's stated impact; the highest priority among the matching classes wins (p0 over p1 over p2). No class matches → use fallback and say so.

classes.description: Data is lost, corrupted or silently overwritten.
Work is blocked and no workaround exists.
A credential, token or private content is exposed, or a security control is bypassed.
A release, deploy or install is broken for users.
Behavior on a supported path that reaches user projects is wrong, and the workaround is costly.
signals: wrong result on a normal run
gate passes when it should fail

classes.description: Behavior is wrong but a cheap, obvious workaround exists.
The defect is in a warning-only or advisory channel that blocks nothing.
signals: false positive in a non-blocking report

classes.description: Only this repository's maintainer tooling is affected; nothing reaches user projects.
Documentation, spec prose or data is inaccurate, with no executable effect.
signals: spec says X, code does Y

classes.description: Presentation only: formatting, naming or output layout.

fallback.reason: The described impact matched no rubric class, so P2 is used rather than guessing higher; raise it if the impact is worse than the description states.
